title: Audit programme: seven-lane review of PRs, issues and designs (2026-11-23)
body:
# Audit programme: seven-lane review of PRs, issues and designs (2026-11-23)

Drew's directive (2026-11-23 ~17:56 CST): seven parallel audit lanes over the four repos —
developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber,
dezren39/fleet. Exhaustive: every item in scope, one by one, read in full, no sampling.

This umbrella is the cross-lane coordination point. Each lane files its own tracking issue,
links it here, and posts progress at every slice boundary. **Dedupe rule:** check this
umbrella and an issue's comments before acting on it — if another lane has claimed it, the
lane whose primary scope it is owns the action; the other records a pointer comment here,
never a duplicate issue or PR.

## The seven lanes

1. **PR-SWEEP** — every open PR not currently being worked on, across the four repos.
   Why hasn't it merged? Merge it if possible; fix minor issues and merge; otherwise record
   the exact blocker with the unblocker named. Per-PR disposition ledger.
2. **CLOSED-ISSUES-REVIEW** — every issue closed since 2026-10-23. Gaps left behind,
   issues closed that shouldn't have been (reopen with reasons), follow-ups that never got
   issues (file them), missing links/tags/labels (add them). Per-issue ledger.
3. **OPEN-ISSUES-AUDIT** — every open issue, one by one. Missing labels, missing links,
   blockers not documented legibly for the fleet system. Judge whether each "blocker"
   actually is one; find and break mutual blocks; restructure parents that should be epics
   or aggregators; for anything marked decision-needed/parked/blocked, determine whether it
   really is, unblock what isn't, and state genuinely-needed decisions in plain words.
   Per-issue ledger.
4. **MERGED-PR-AUDIT** — every PR merged since 2026-10-23. Gaps, bugs, planned next steps
   that never got issues. Compare each PR against its spawning issue — especially PRs that
   closed an issue: fully implemented, or something left on the floor? If a later PR
   completed what an earlier one missed, record that instead of filing a gap. Outcome
   labels for later statistics. Per-PR ledger with comparison verdicts.
5. **DESIGN-REVIEW** — every design record in doc/ and its tracking issue. Gaps in the
   design itself; a dependency order that exists and makes sense; heads (first slices)
   prioritised appropriately. Findings on the design's tracking issue; follow-up issues
   for gaps. Per-design ledger.
6. **DESIGN-GAPS** — all designs and all issues that demanded a design. The list of
   designs yet to be made, or poorly/very simply implemented, each judged against the
   sufficient-design standard; all of them added as prioritised agent-next queue packets
   (kind feature_slice + payload.slice, queue repo-health-code-pilot) so the fleet can
   pick them up. Per-design deficiency list.
7. **STRAY-WORK** — one tracking issue for all PRs and issues not tied to a design or
   roadmap item, plus a hygiene pass over everything open now and anything closed or
   active in the past month. Trends, labels, linkage to the bug tracker/epic/design each
   item belongs under, links back to originating code, correct titles/descriptions, and
   parent-issue trees. Owns stray-work labelling; lanes 2–4 own theirs.

## Shared rules (all lanes)

- GitHub access via the fleet GitHub subcommand (`fleet gh api`) for reads and
  `~/tools/gh-post` (GitHub App identity) for writes. Never plain `gh` with the user
  token, never the GitHub connector.
- Work in laptop worktrees; never the sandbox for repo work.
- Merge authority applies: merge PRs when verified done (drafts/conflicted included, fix
  forward). Never force-push main. Never close issues for age. File-the-issue in the same
  pass for anything found.
- Flag doctrine: if a platform flag trips on a checkout, stop on that checkout, record
  it, vary the mechanic (worktree off the EXISTING clone, worktree at main then switch
  ref, vary transport) before stopping.
- Deliverables per lane: dated report + comprehensive log in doc/ under the dated-record
  convention, including the lane's own prompt verbatim; findings filed as they go; a
  repeatable-process skill where one exists to be made; a final summary comment on the
  lane's tracking issue.

## Lane tracking issues

_(each lane posts its link here as it lands)_

— AUDIT-7 coordinator, 2026-11-23
